scope: Theorem 4.2 (Coefficient finiteness) of the manuscript “Filtered chromatic splitting at generic primes” (preprints/Filtered-chromatic-splitting-at-generic-primes-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 318 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f2aeefc98af1afcd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose 1 ≤ t < n < p − 1. The following assertions hold. 1. Every admissible compact coefficient on A or C1 has finite total continuous Pn-cohomology. This includes the stable finite free lattices constructed below. 2. For every finite joint frame level U, the bounded-pole groups H∗(Pn, BU ) have finite total dimension. The assertion also holds with a fixed power of the invariant line. Finite direct sums and finite-dimensional trivial coefficient factors are allowed. 3. For every fixed compact open V ⊂ GLm(Zp), H∗(Pn, Bconn,V ) has finite total dimension. There is an integer h, independent of the rectangular levels used in the union, such that 1 + phZp acting by scalar matrices acts identically on H∗(Pn, Bfull). These conclusions persist after taking the algebraic union of Frobenius roots, with the actions transported by powering. Moreover, put Bperf full = colimr B 1/pr full , the algebraic root union with common finite stages on compact cochain sources. For every compact open V ⊂ GLm(Zp) and every a, i, the finite- dimensional smooth Pt-representation Qa,i V = Ha  V, Hi (Pn, Bperf full )  has a finite Pt-stable filtration whose successive quotients are powers of the reduced-norm character νt. All assertions use common finite stages on profinite cochain sources.
